correctness.rationale: For sufficiently small translations the polygon support-normal fan persists; the intersection area is exactly quadratic in inward offsets d_i(u)=(-n_i·u)_+. Integrating directional positive-cosine first/second/adjacent products gives linear coefficient −2Lr³/3 and quartic coefficient Σ[1+(π−α_i)cot α_i]r⁴/8, then r=ρ√(A/π) yields the dimensionless formula. The angle function f(a)=1+(π−a)cot a satisfies f″(a)=2(sin β−β cos β)/sin³β>2/3, so strict Jensen on f(a)−a²/3 with Σα=(N−2)π gives equality only equiangular. A centrally symmetric N=2m turning-angle family with four ±ε deviations and ε=1/(5N) sends the excess/Σdeviation² ratio to 1/(24π²). The independent square check yields C4=1/(2π²), and symbolic derivative confirms the strict-curvature formula.
residual_risks: Fan persistence gives a polygon-dependent positive radius, not a uniform radius; no global distance-distribution comparison for large ρ follows.

value.rationale: The next local coefficient beyond the perimeter term isolates angle geometry, a natural stochastic geometric invariant of convex polygons. The proof determines its complete N-vertex minimizing class, a quantitative squared-angle rigidity inequality and the strongest possible side-count-uniform coefficient. These are meaningful structural extremal results independent of any downstream theorem and not recomputation of a shape table.
residual_risks: The sharp variance factor is uniform across N; fixed-N best constants are not determined.

final_claim: For every N>=3 convex polygon the normalized short-pair probability is exactly quartic for sufficiently small radius, with C4=Σ[1+(π−α)cot α]/(8π²), and C4 has the sharp all-N angle-variance lower bound with best universal coefficient 1/(24π²), equality precisely at equiangular polygons.
limitations: Local small-radius identity only, not for all separations.
Older general polygon distance formulas can recover particular-shape coefficients; full Baltzis article inaccessible.
